judge.diversity_evidence: All stories use the same library problem and resolution: Jun’s missing whale book is searched for, found high on a shelf with a bookmark, retrieved by Ms Alvarez, and read. Most (including s000014 and s000028) also check out Mina’s atlas; a smaller branch (including s000058 and s000023) has Mina set the atlas aside and help Jun instead. These are minor variations, not substantially different plots. The sample does not establish the diversity of the entire generator.

judge.diversity_evidence: All 20 stories share the same core problem and causal sequence: Bea makes a cup for Grandpa’s stiff hand, a slipped tool dents it, and she finishes and gives it to him. The only meaningful branch is whether she explicitly turns the dent into a thumb rest, as in s000014, s000021, s000034, s000042, s000039, s000035, and s000024, or merely smooths the dent and leaves its usefulness unconfirmed, as in s000058, s000023, s000036, s000017, s000053, s000048, s000002, s000057, s000038, s000018, s000007, and s000041. Variations in wording or order of returning tools do not create distinct plots. This sample alone does not establish the diversity of the whole generator.

plot_groups.summary: While making a cup for Grandpa’s stiff hand, Bea accidentally dents it, then reshapes the dent into a thumb rest; after firing and glazing the cup, Grandpa uses the rest to hold it.
Bea makes and finishes a cup for Grandpa’s stiff hand after accidentally denting it, but only smooths the dent; Grandpa receives the cup without the story showing the dent as a useful aid.
